description: Our team is tackling the challenge of highlighting the hardware and equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. We want to tell the stories of these silent rovers, landers, and descent stages—not as space junk, but as humanity’s first historic monuments in deep space. Our goal is to create a compelling narrative or visual project that honors these machines and reminds people of the incredible human effort behind them.
summary:
Explorers-101 is an educational website made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It showcases spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific equipment left on the Moon, Mars, asteroids and in deep space after their missions ended. Although these machines may no longer be working, they remain important symbols of exploration and human curiosity.

We created "Silent Explorers of the Cosmos: Humanity’s Off-World Monuments," an interactive experience featuring a 3D spacecraft hangar, searchable hardware catalogue, sound experiences, science simulations and a multi-level quiz. Visitors can explore models of spacecraft like the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, Pioneer 10, Kepler/K2 and the Ingenuity helicopter. The catalogue features eleven off-world monuments across different destinations.

Our simulations make space science engaging. Users can explore the Mars Pathfinder airbag landing, understand how Kepler detects exoplanets through changes in starlight, compare gravity on the Moon and Earth, and experience recreations of Martian wind and lunar impacts. A quiz allows visitors to test their knowledge.

Our project transforms mission history and technical information into an interactive learning experience. Rather than presenting retired hardware as forgotten equipment, Explorers-101 celebrates it as part of humanity's legacy in space. We hope to inspire students and curious visitors to explore space science, appreciate past missions and imagine the possibilities of future exploration.
details:
Explorers-101 is an educational website that shows spacecraft, rovers, landers and scientific equipment that were left on the Moon, Mars, asteroids and in deep space. It has interactive 3D models, a searchable hardware catalogue, scientific simulations, sound experiences and quizzes to make space exploration fun and easy to understand. Our goal is to help students and visitors see the importance of these machines to appreciate past achievements and to think of them as lasting symbols of human exploration instead of things that were left behind and forgotten.

We made the website using Visual Studio Code and Antigravity AI while using NASAs space resources and internet research to collect information explore ideas and guide development. AI was used for help with coding and solving technical problems; the research, planning, ideas, creative choices and the whole project were done by our team. Our creativity is in turning information into an interactive learning experience. During the process we thought about educational value, correct information, easy access, fun, for users and simple way to move around the website.
